text:
Building patient trust doesn't require repeatedly explaining qualifications, specialization, or being a professor. As a patient, all I wanted was a clear treatment plan!

Personally, I was ready to follow all of the doctor's instructions. If they didn't want to use X-rays from elsewhere, I was willing to get new ones and had signed the consent form, ready to start treatment as soon as the X-rays were done. However, after a lengthy discussion, I was told that the patient didn't understand, even though I was confident I understood everything the doctor explained.

Ultimately, I decided not to continue treatment there because I didn't know what further questions the doctor was looking for. It felt like the communication was more focused on the doctor's expertise than on a clear treatment plan.

text:
Six months later,

I'm downgrading my rating.

I arrived at the clinic about 15 minutes before my appointment time (12:00 PM).

The staff were lovely and provided excellent service. However, upon arrival, I realized I might be a bit late because the previous patient was late.

After waiting for a while, the staff kindly checked the time and then came back to inform me that I should come back at 1:30 PM (an hour and a half late!).

In the end, I had to cancel my appointment because I had other plans.

✨ A heartfelt suggestion:
I understand that sometimes, unforeseen circumstances can cause delays. However, if you know you're likely to be late (because the previous patient was late), it would be great if you could call or Line the clinic to let them know before they arrive. A little advance notice would help you manage your time better and avoid wasting time traveling back and forth to the clinic and having to cancel. 😊
